root_cause: The datepicker formats the input value using the locale when the dateFormat option is not set, causing the value to change from ISO format to locale-specific format (e.g., MM/DD/YYYY in en-US) even when the user does not select a new date.
repair_strategy: Change the default dateFormat option in the datepicker to return the date in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD) using the local timezone, ensuring the input value remains in the expected format regardless of locale.

edits.before:
dateFormat: null, // Intl.DateTimeFormat options, or function(date, locale) => string
  displayElement: null, // Element to show formatted date (defaults to element for buttons)
  displayMonthsCount: 1, // Number of months to display side-by-side

expected_accessibility_effect: This change does not affect accessibility directly, as it only changes the format of the date in the input field. The datepicker keyboard interaction remains unchanged.
functional_risks: If there are any display elements associated with the datepicker (via the displayElement option), they will now show the date in ISO format instead of the locale format, which may not be desired.
The change affects all datepickers in the application that rely on the default dateFormat.
verification_requirements: Verify that the departure date input retains its initial ISO format value (2026-10-22) after opening and closing the datepicker without selecting a date.
Verify that when a date is selected, the input value is updated to the selected date in ISO format.
Verify that the form submission includes the departure date in ISO format (e.g., departure=2026-10-22).
